about.title: About
about.heroLine: A first-year PPE student who got tired of spreadsheets
about.story1: Pakamon was born out of real frustration. At the start of my first year in PPE at Tel Aviv University, I tried to figure out how many courses I needed, from which discipline, and what the prerequisites were. The Yedion is an ASP.NET table from the 2000s. The regulations are a PDF nobody reads to the end. And there's no tool that connects the two.
about.story2: So I built Pakamon. Not as a final project and not as a startup — just because I needed it. After a few weeks, friends from the program asked for access. Then their friends. Now it's here, open to everyone.
about.whatIs: Pakamon is a degree planning tool for PPE at Tel Aviv University. It helps organize 150 credits across 3 years, track regulation compliance, calculate your graduation score, and build a weekly schedule — without opening the Yedion every time.
about.notList1: Not a commercial product — no subscription, no ads
about.notList2: Not official — not affiliated with the university. Always verify with the secretary's office
about.notList3: Not perfect — there are bugs, there are missing things. If you find something, let me know
about.contact: Questions, bugs, ideas? Write to me:

faq.title: FAQ
faq.subtitle: Questions my friends from the program kept asking
faq.a1: No. Pakamon helps plan and track, but it doesn't replace the secretary's office or the academic advisor. Always verify critical decisions (like year transitions or course deferrals) with the official source.
faq.a2: Courses are based on the 2026-27 Yedion — including the timetable, groups and rooms. The 2026-27 exam schedule isn't published by the university yet, so it isn't shown here. If something looks off — check the Yedion and let me know.
faq.q3: Can I take a seminar outside my discipline?
faq.a3: Yes, but there are limits. In Economics you can take a maximum of 2 seminars, and you can't have more than 2 seminars with the same lecturer. Credits count toward the course's discipline, not your focus area.
faq.q4: What happens if I fail a course?
faq.a4: Mark the course as "Failed" in your plan. The credits won't count, the grade won't factor into your average, and you'll need to replan. Pakamon will show you the impact on regulation compliance.
faq.a5: On Supabase servers (AWS in Europe). I can't see your password, I don't share data with anyone, and I don't sell anything. Full details on the Privacy page.
faq.q6: I'm not in PPE. Are there other programs?
faq.a6: Currently Pakamon is built only for PPE at Tel Aviv University. I'm planning to expand to other programs in the future — if you have a program you'd like supported, write to me.
faq.a7: Free. Completely. No subscription, no ads, no "upgrade to pro". I built it because I needed it.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Pakamon respects user privacy. Here's exactly what we collect, why, and what we don't do.
privacy.collect1: Email and password (encrypted) — for registration and login
privacy.collect3: Your study plan — courses, grades, semesters
privacy.collect4: Personal preferences — study year, focus area, miluim group
privacy.dontCollect1: No browsing tracking, no third-party cookies
privacy.dontCollect2: No Google Analytics, no Facebook Pixel, no tracking cookies, no ads. The only usage measurement is Vercel's anonymous page counting (no cookies, no personal identifiers, no cross-site tracking) — so we know which screens help.
privacy.dontCollect3: We don't sell data to anyone, ever
privacy.storage: Data is stored on Supabase (AWS servers in Europe). Passwords are encrypted. Communication is encrypted via TLS.
privacy.google: If you choose to connect Google Calendar, we only access your calendar for schedule syncing. We don't read existing events, don't access emails, and don't share the data. You can disconnect anytime from Settings.
privacy.delete: Want everything gone? Settings → Account has a permanent-delete button — it immediately removes all your data: profile, plan, grades, and your anonymous contributions, insights and published plans. No questions, no waiting.
privacy.ai: When you ask the advisor or scan a document (grade sheet / Form 3010), that text or photo is sent to Google Gemini for processing — only then, and only that. Your personal key (if added) is stored encrypted. Nothing is sent to AI in the background.
privacy.cohort: If you chose to share grades or ratings — they're stored as anonymous points with no name and no way to trace the contributor, shown only as averages once enough people contribute. Insights and plans you publish to the cohort file appear without your name — only your class year — and can be deleted anytime.

accessibility.title: Accessibility Statement
accessibility.intro: Pakamon is built so that as many students as possible can use it — including those who browse with a keyboard only or with a screen reader. This is an ongoing effort, and we keep improving.
accessibility.done1: All main screens were scanned with an automated tool (axe) and fixed down to zero high-severity issues.
accessibility.done2: Every action — including course dragging and the exam board — is fully keyboard-accessible, with a clear focus indicator.
accessibility.done3: Every button and field has an accessible name for screen readers, and color contrast meets WCAG 2.1 level AA.
accessibility.done4: The site fully supports right-to-left Hebrew and left-to-right English.
accessibility.limits: Some complex components (like charts and drag boards) may not yet offer a complete screen-reader experience. If you hit a problem — we'd love to hear and fix it.
accessibility.contact: Write to us and we'll take care of it promptly:

degreeInfo.focusAreaExplanation: The focus area determines your civil service classification. You need at least 60 credits in one discipline to be classified in that field.
degreeInfo.eachPaperWeight: Each seminar paper = ~6% of the final degree grade
degreeInfo.maxEconSeminars: Max {maxEcon} seminars in Economics, max 2 seminars with the same lecturer
degreeInfo.coursesInEnglish: Courses taught in English (any discipline, min {min} credits each)
degreeInfo.englishTip: Tip: some mandatory courses (like "Introduction to Moral Philosophy") can be taken in English too — so they also count toward the English requirement.

glossary.shasDef: Semester hours — the degree's counting unit. You need 150 to graduate.
glossary.seminarDef: An advanced course where you write a research paper. You need 4 across the degree.
glossary.referatDef: A shorter seminar paper — counts as 4% of the degree grade.
glossary.focusDef: The discipline you specialize in (60 credits) — sets your civil-service classification.
glossary.levelDef: Preparatory English courses that don't count toward the 150, based on your Amirant score.
glossary.exemptDef: No level courses needed. You still need 2 English content courses.

miluim.howToRealize: Most benefits apply automatically (exam-date choice, bidding). Credit exemptions require a request — contact the reserves office or Dean of Students. To mark a course binary (pass/fail): on the course card in the planner, for a completed course with a grade. Update your service data here so the system calculates correctly.
